_readme: NEW JERSEY PROPERTY TAX APPEAL OUTCOMES, by county, by year.
From the Division of Taxation Summary of Property Tax Appeals, filed annually
under N.J.S.A. 54:3-5.1. This is the only published record of what actually
happens to tax appeals in New Jersey, and it exists as a stack of PDFs.
THE DATA IS COUNTY LEVEL, NOT MUNICIPAL. There is no public town by town
breakdown. That is less of a limitation than it sounds: appeals are heard by
the COUNTY board of taxation, so the county is the body whose behaviour you are
actually predicting when you ask "what happens if I file".
A win means the assessment came down, either revised by the board after a
hearing or stipulated by agreement beforehand. Most successful appeals settle,
so counting only revisions would understate success badly.
win_rate_filed    wins as a share of every appeal filed
win_rate_decided  wins as a share of appeals that got a decision on the merits,
residential       class 2 appeals, which is what a homeowner files
Keyed by 2 digit county code, the first two characters of any PAMS PIN.
source: NJ Division of Taxation, Summary of Property Tax Appeals
